textual.observation: The speaker describes paid Bitcoin-mining contracts, including a $100 offer said to generate Bitcoins daily and a $10,000 contract said to provide more Bitcoin and commissions.

evidence.quote: It proposes 3 contrats. We have a $ 100 offer It will allow us to mine bitcoins a mining rate of three THB per second. You can generate this power by miners. They will then be able to generate bitcoins to you daily.

contract costs more... more time and money... which costs $10,000 it's the one who offers more land to the person and so the one who will see earning more Bitcoin. And the commissions will be, as you said, more $5,000.

textual.context: The description presents Coinomia as an investment program, while the ASR presents the contracts as part of a business launch. The source records do not establish whether the stated mining activity, returns or commissions occurred.
textual.potential_relevance: The source links payment for contracts to promised Bitcoin generation and stated commissions, including a higher-cost tier, which may require later assessment of the offer's conditions and substantiation.
textual.limitations: The records do not verify the company, mining operations, contract terms, payment recipients, actual returns or whether the figures are guarantees.

textual.observation: The speaker describes an MLM structure in which recruiting people into lower levels is associated with receiving more money and team-based commissions.

evidence.quote: You get girls from different levels The higher the level Then once you are down to lower level, you will have to recruit more employees... and you will get more money.
there are commission to the VDIs and Binary commissions the commissions generated by the entire team

textual.context: The speaker is explaining the MLM model as part of the presentation. The ASR contains transcription errors, including the phrase "You get girls".
textual.potential_relevance: The source explicitly connects recruiting additional people and team activity with increased money or commissions, creating a recruitment-and-reward relationship for later context assessment.
textual.limitations: The records do not establish the actual compensation rules, legality, participant outcomes or whether the described commissions were paid.

textual.observation: The speaker instructs viewers to use a description link, enter an address and name, and share an invitation link so another user subscribes.

evidence.quote: you can click on the link at the description then now, go on that page about this click on it open a web page to see that text there is the same page we must uncheck it We have to select them. Then enter the address and then enter this name
If you invite someone, you have the same interface and you send this name and after, share this link with your other user to see their presence so that they do subscribe

textual.context: The instructions appear within the business presentation and are followed by a statement about inviting another user. The records do not clarify what address or name is requested or what the linked page does.
textual.potential_relevance: The source links clicking a destination and submitting an address and name with inviting another user to subscribe, so the requested data and recruitment flow may require later assessment.
textual.limitations: No URL, form fields, permissions, recipient, transaction result or external-page content is supplied, and the source does not establish that any information was submitted.

visual.observation: A website presents Bitcoin and Ethereum mining contracts priced at $100, $1,000, and $10,000, with stated mining-power figures and a "Sign Up Now!" control.
visual.context: The visible page appears to promote mining-contract purchases in an ordinary commercial presentation; the supplied frames do not establish whether the services or returns are genuine.
visual.potential_relevance: A promised mining-related return is presented alongside requests to purchase one of several paid contract tiers, creating a reward/payment relationship that may merit review.
visual.limitations: These frames do not establish payment completion, actual mining activity, payout outcomes, or whether the displayed figures are guaranteed.

visual.observation: The site displays direct referral commissions of 8%, 10%, and 12% for the contract tiers, and a dashboard calculates commission amounts based on referred users or contracts.
visual.context: The commission information is shown as part of a multi-level marketing presentation and account dashboard.
visual.potential_relevance: Commission returns are explicitly linked to recruiting or referring other users and to contract purchases, which is a task-relevant recruitment/payment relationship.
visual.limitations: The frames do not show whether anyone was actually recruited, paid, or financially harmed, and they do not establish the terms beyond the visible calculations.

visual.observation: A dashboard shows an "Estimated Paycheck on Launch Day" of $36,200.00 and calculated mining payouts of $100,000.00 for selected contract quantities.
visual.context: The amounts are labeled as estimated or calculated figures within a dashboard; the introductory frame also references a planned launch date.
visual.potential_relevance: Large stated or estimated returns are associated with a future launch and selected contract quantities, making the return/timeframe relationship potentially relevant for review.
visual.limitations: The sampled frames do not establish that the amounts were promised as guaranteed, that the launch occurred, or that any payout was received.

visual.observation: The account-creation page requests sponsor information, user ID, name, country, email, password, and password confirmation before an apparent mining-start action.
visual.context: The form is presented as a new-account registration page for the same visibly branded mining site.
visual.potential_relevance: Submitting identifying and account-credential information is linked to creating an account for access to the promoted mining activity and referral structure.
visual.limitations: The frames do not show submission, data handling, payment authorization, or any resulting account access.

textual_context_notes.observation: The title characterizes the material as a prelaunch MLM presentation involving Bitcoin.

evidence.quote: Coinomia Presentation French | Prelaunch MLM Mixed With Bitcoin

textual_context_notes.observation: The description frames the speaker's assessment as an opinion.
The speaker says the opportunity was proposed by a friend and describes personal unfamiliarity with this type of investing.

evidence.quote: I am not too much of this kind of investing but there it is one friend who proposed this plan and that I found very interesting

visual_context_notes.observation: The opening slide visibly refers to a French-language presentation about an MLM associated with Bitcoin and a planned launch date of November 1.
The dashboard contains navigation items including "My Team" and "Your Referral Links," alongside mining and income panels.

annotation.contextual_rationale: This video is scam content because it promotes paid Coinomia Bitcoin-mining contracts, with higher-priced tiers presented as generating more Bitcoin and commissions. It invites participation through signup controls, recruitment and team activity tied to earnings, and links for sharing and joining. The account page does not show submission, payment, actual mining, or realized payouts, and the displayed estimates are not established as guaranteed.
annotation.fine_grained_rationale: The central offer is purchasing mining contracts at different price levels in exchange for Bitcoin mining output and daily returns. The presentation also promotes team and binary commissions tied to recruitment, supporting S06 as a secondary mechanism.

evidence.observation: The narration identifies a mining contract costing $10,000.
The narration links the mining power from the contracts to daily Bitcoin generation.
evidence.quote: They will then be able to generate bitcoins to you daily.

evidence.observation: The dashboard visibly shows 'Binary Commission For - 23 Users & 11 Pairs' alongside mining payouts and a calculated estimated income.
The speaker describes recruiting additional people as a way to receive more money.
evidence.quote: you will have to recruit more employees... and you will get more money.

evidence.observation: The displayed Coinomia account-creation form contains ordinary registration fields, including email, name, country, password, and password confirmation.
